# AIFactory 0.3.0 — deterministic design authority

AIFactory 0.3.0 adds a design-authority spine to the experimental autonomous
builder. Architecture is represented as strict Design IR v1, checked against
the exact parent Contract and effective runner capabilities, evaluated by a
deterministic gate, and bound to explicit human approval before implementation.

## Highlights

- Strict Design IR v1 validation, canonical digests, immutable generations,
  exact Contract parentage, and exact Design approval.
- Conservative runner capability assessment: runtime observation can remove a
  declared guarantee but cannot add one.
- Bounded SARIF and native harness analyzers with normalized, replayable
  evidence and fail-closed routing.
- New `factory design`, `factory analyze`, `factory capabilities`, and
  `factory status` command surfaces with versioned JSON output.
- A shared publication verifier covering legacy and Design workflows.
- Opt-in migration per new Contract parent, sticky workflow selection, and
  rollback through a later new parent without rewriting prior authority.

## Compatibility and limits

The autonomous builder remains experimental and human supervision remains the
recommended path for important work. Schema validity is not design correctness,
analyzers can miss defects, installed analyzers are trusted code, directory
separation is not an OS sandbox, and local approval identity is not a
cryptographic signature. Native Windows analyzer execution is unsupported.

This is a source-only GitHub release; it is not published on PyPI.

Install the tagged source directly from GitHub:

```bash
pip install "git+https://github.com/BrainMatterStudios/AIFactory.git@0.3.0"
```

Read the [complete release notes](https://github.com/BrainMatterStudios/AIFactory/blob/0.3.0/docs/releases/0.3.0.md) for migration guidance, the macOS no-atime limitation, the threat model, provenance, and explicit non-claims.
